# Use skill-review

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Audit an existing Agent Skill folder (SKILL.md plus its scripts, references and evals) for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Kiro or Antigravity, and return a READY / FIX FIRST / REWRITE verdict with severity-tagged findings across five areas — whether a router would pick it and whether it collides with a sibling, portability, safety (mapped to the OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10), structure, and eval coverage — backed by a stdlib lint script for the mechanical checks.

**Reach for it when** the user says "review this skill", "is my SKILL.md any good", "why doesn't my skill trigger", "is this skill safe to install", or wants a skill checked before sharing or publishing it.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install skill-review                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install skill-review --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install skill-review --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Skill engineering pack: [`--pack skill-engineering`](../packs/use-the-skill-engineering-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/skill-engineering/skills/skill-review/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Review this SKILL.md before I share it with my team"
- "My skill never triggers in Codex. Can you audit the folder and tell me why?"
- "Is this third-party skill safe to install? Check its scripts and instructions"
- "Lint my agent skill and give me a ready or not verdict"
- "Check whether my Claude Code skill will work in Copilot and Kiro too"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Write a new skill that turns support tickets into a weekly digest"
- "Generate eval cases for my existing skill so I can catch regressions"
- "Audit our repo's AGENTS.md; agents keep running commands that don't exist"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use skill-review".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **The verdict follows the rules in step 9**, and the counts in the verdict line match the findings below it.
- **Lint output is pasted verbatim**, and every lint ERROR either appears as a finding or is explained away in one line.
- **Every finding has a location and a concrete fix.** "Improve the description" is not a fix. The rewritten sentence is.
- **Collision findings name the sibling and the query** that would route wrongly.
- **Safety findings carry an AST ID** and say what the line makes the agent do, not just which pattern matched.
- **Judgment goes beyond the lint.** At least one finding, or an explicit "nothing beyond the lint", covers what the regexes can't see: routing, paraphrased safety issues, steps that don't decide.
- **It reviews the skill, not the task.** Whether release notes should exist is out of scope. Whether this skill writes them reliably is the job.

## Use something else when

- Writing a new skill from a task description: use `skill-author`
- Adding a skill to the skilldrop catalogue itself, which has its own manifest and `validate.py` rules: follow that repo's `AGENTS.md` and run `python3 validate.py`
- Generating more eval cases for a skill whose only gap is coverage: use `eval-harness-generator`
- Reviewing a repo's always-on AGENTS.md policy file: use `agents-md-generator`
- Threat-modelling the agent deployment that runs skills (its tools, data and egress): use `agent-threat-model`
- Critiquing an ordinary document such as an ADR or design doc: use `doc-critique`
